intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the Arctic sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind this magical phenomenon.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic geothermal hot spring surrounded by dramatic lava fields. The milky-blue mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin-healing silica and algae. Book the Comfort package to include a silica mud mask and a welcome drink.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents, offering an authentic and affordable soak in the Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Glacier Hiking on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the stunning Sólheimajökull glacier with a certified guide. Trek across ice formations, peer into vivid blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. A thrilling activity that pairs perfectly with the surrounding volcanic scenery.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and rich Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, and fresh seafood, while visiting landmarks such as Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and baggage claim, then take the Flybus or a shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: Flybus is significantly cheaper than a taxi). Check in, settle into your beachfront room, and get a good night's rest after your journey.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack or sandwich from the airport convenience store upon arrival to save money on your first night

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means very limited daylight (roughly 5-6 hours). Temperatures can be near or below freezing. Pack warm, layered clothing. The Flybus from Keflavik to Reykjavik area costs around 3,000-4,000 ISK per person, far cheaper than a private taxi. Keep your eyes open for the Northern Lights even on the drive from the airport if skies are clear.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a leisurely start, walk along the beachfront near the resort to take in the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery. Explore the immediate surroundings and get oriented. Sunrise is around 11:00 AM in January, so there is no rush to be up early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik city center (accessible by bus or rideshare). Visit Hallgrimskirkja Church (free to enter the exterior and grounds; small fee for the tower). Walk down Skolavordustigur street and explore the colorful houses. Stroll along Laugavegur, the main shopping street, window shopping and soaking up local culture without spending much.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area before dark. After dinner, bundle up and step outside or find an open field near the resort for your first Northern Lights watch. Check aurora forecast apps like Vedur.is (Iceland Met Office) for activity levels. Clear skies and a KP index of 2 or higher give good chances.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort or pick up groceries from a nearby Bonus or Kronan supermarket (Iceland's budget supermarket chains) to stock up for the trip
meals.lunch: Reykjavik hot dog from Baejarins Beztu Pylsur, the famous hot dog stand in the city center — an iconic and very affordable Icelandic meal under 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the resort kitchen if available, or try Hlolla Batar, a budget-friendly submarine sandwich shop in Reykjavik

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on groceries at Bonus supermarket today — this is the single biggest money-saving tip for Iceland. Cooking your own breakfasts and some dinners can cut food costs by 50% or more. Download the Vedur.is aurora forecast app immediately.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to the famous Golden Circle route. Start with Thingvellir National Park (free entry), a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá gorge and admire the frozen or partially frozen landscape in January. Daylight is precious, so start as early as possible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to Geysir Geothermal Area (free to visit the geysers). Watch Strokkur erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting boiling water up to 30 meters. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall (free), one of Iceland's most iconic waterfalls, which may have stunning ice formations in January.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort. Stop at a roadside viewpoint on the way back for another Northern Lights attempt. The Golden Circle area, away from city lights, is excellent for aurora viewing. Check the forecast before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from your Bonus grocery haul to eat at Thingvellir or Geysir — this saves significant money compared to tourist-area restaurants
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the resort, or try Mandi, an affordable Middle Eastern restaurant in Reykjavik if passing through

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for several days is actually cost-effective when split among travelers and gives full flexibility. Budget car rentals from companies like Sad Cars or Geysir Car Rental start around 5,000-8,000 ISK per day in January. Check road conditions at Road.is before every drive. The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km total.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula, close to the resort and Keflavik area. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (free), a small footbridge symbolizing the gap between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Walk around the Reykjanes Geopark volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon area — instead of paying the expensive Blue Lagoon entrance fee, explore the surrounding lava fields and geothermal landscape for free from the outside. Alternatively, visit the nearby Grindavik town for a coastal walk. For a budget hot spring experience, research smaller local pools in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Keflavik town for a walk along the harbor. Return to the resort for dinner. If skies are clear, tonight is another excellent Northern Lights opportunity — the Reykjanes Peninsula has minimal light pollution in many areas. Set an alarm for midnight and check the aurora app.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort
meals.lunch: Pick up lunch from a gas station (N1 or Orkan) — Icelandic gas stations have surprisingly good and affordable hot food like lamb soup, hot dogs, and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon requires advance booking and costs 7,000-15,000 ISK or more per person — not ideal for a budget trip. Later in the itinerary we will visit more affordable hot springs. The Reykjanes area is geologically very active and fascinating to explore for free.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast of Iceland. Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (small parking fee, roughly 700 ISK). In summer you can walk behind it, but in January icy conditions may restrict access — still stunning from the front. Nearby is the hidden Gljufrabui waterfall, tucked inside a canyon, which is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skogafoss Waterfall (free). Climb the staircase to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast. Continue to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara (free) near Vik, with its dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves — they are very dangerous here.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back westward toward the resort, or if you have booked accommodation further east, stay near Vik. Stop at a dark area on the drive back for Northern Lights viewing. The South Coast offers spectacular aurora backdrops with waterfalls and snow-covered landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure — this is a long driving day
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from grocery supplies eaten at Skogafoss or Reynisfjara
meals.dinner: Sudur-Vik restaurant in Vik offers affordable Icelandic meals, or grab soup from a gas station on the drive back

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast round trip from Reykjavik is approximately 350-400 km. Start no later than 10:00 AM to make the most of daylight (roughly 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM in January). Road conditions can be challenging — always check Road.is. This is one of the most scenic drives in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day or local exploration near the resort. Sleep in after several busy driving days. Take a leisurely morning walk along the beachfront. Visit a local swimming pool (sundlaug) — Iceland's public swimming pools with hot pots are extremely affordable (around 1,000-1,200 ISK) and a beloved local tradition. The Keflavik area has Sundholl Reykjanesbaer pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Viking World Museum in Njarðvik near Keflavik (small entry fee, around 2,000 ISK). It houses a full-scale replica Viking ship and exhibits on Norse history. Alternatively, explore the Keflavik harbor area and the Duus Museum complex for local art and maritime history.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights dedicated evening. After an early dinner, drive to a dark spot on the Reykjanes Peninsula away from town lights. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate, warm blankets, and your camera on a tripod. Stay out for 1-2 hours scanning the sky. January is peak aurora season in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort
meals.lunch: Affordable meal at a local bakery (bakari) — Icelandic bakeries offer fresh bread, pastries, and soup at reasonable prices
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort — try making skyr with fruit and oats, a traditional Icelandic dairy product available cheaply at Bonus

day_by_day.notes: Public swimming pools (sundlaugar) are Iceland's social hubs and an authentic cultural experience. They are far more affordable than tourist spa experiences. The hot pots (heitir pottar) outside are typically 38-44°C. Shower thoroughly before entering as per Icelandic custom — this is strictly enforced.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula if you have a rental car — it is about a 2-hour drive from Reykjavik. Visit Snæfellsjokull National Park (free entry). The glacier-capped volcano Snæfellsjokull inspired Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Walk around Djupalonssandur black pebble beach (free) with dramatic sea stacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the peninsula to Arnarstapi and Hellnar, small fishing villages with stunning coastal lava formations and bird cliffs (free to explore). Walk the coastal path between the two villages (about 2.5 km). Visit Budakirkja, the famous black church, for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward the resort. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula has very dark skies — if the aurora forecast is favorable, pull over at any dark roadside area for viewing. Return to the resort by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the long drive
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Djupalonssandur beach or Arnarstapi
meals.dinner: Fjoruhusid cafe in Hellnar is a charming option for soup and light meals, or self-catered dinner back at the resort

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is often called Iceland in miniature because it has glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, hot springs, and dramatic coastlines all in one area. The full loop is about 200 km. Check weather carefully — the peninsula can have severe weather. This is a long but very rewarding day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Fludir, approximately 1.5 hours from Reykjavik. This is Iceland's oldest swimming pool and one of the most affordable natural hot spring experiences, costing around 2,800-3,000 ISK — significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the geothermal pool surrounded by geysers and steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at Kerid Volcanic Crater (entry fee around 700 ISK), a stunning red and black volcanic crater with a vivid teal lake at the bottom. Walk the rim for panoramic views. Also stop at Skalholt Cathedral (free), one of Iceland's oldest religious sites with historical significance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Spend the evening relaxing and warming up after outdoor activities. Check aurora forecast for tonight — if KP index is 3 or above and skies are clear, venture out for aurora hunting around 21:00-23:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a gas station N1 for affordable hot soup — Fludir area has limited dining options
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort, or try Gamla Bakarinn (The Old Bakery) in Selfoss town on the way back for affordable sandwiches and pastries

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is the best budget alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Book in advance online as it can sell out even in January. Bring your own towel to save the rental fee. The water temperature is around 38-40°C year-round. Combining with Kerid Crater makes for an efficient and affordable day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik more deeply. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnamssyningin) — a fascinating underground museum built around actual Viking Age ruins discovered beneath the city. Entry is around 2,200 ISK. Alternatively, the National Museum of Iceland (Thjodminjasafn) offers comprehensive Icelandic history for around 2,500 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Perlan building on Oskjuhlid hill (free to walk around outside, small fee for the observation deck). Enjoy panoramic views of Reykjavik and surrounding mountains. Walk down through Oskjuhlid forest. Visit Tjornin lake in the city center (free) — often partially frozen in January with photogenic reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Reykjavik's famous geothermal hot pot culture at Laugardalslaug, the largest public pool in Iceland. It has multiple hot pots, a large outdoor swimming pool, and a water slide. Entry is around 1,200 ISK. Afterward, grab dinner in the Laugardalur area.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters cafe for affordable coffee and a light lunch, or Sandholt Bakery for fresh Icelandic bread and pastries
meals.dinner: Noodle Station on Skolavordustigur — one of Reykjavik's best budget restaurants, offering hearty noodle soups for around 1,800-2,200 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik's public swimming pools are open year-round and are genuinely one of the best budget experiences in Iceland. Laugardalslaug also has a botanical garden adjacent to it (free in summer, limited in winter). The Reykjavik City Card offers discounts on museums and public transport if you plan multiple museum visits.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Hveragerdi area, about 45 minutes from Reykjavik. This geothermal town sits on extremely active ground. Visit the Hveragerdi Geothermal Park in town (small entry fee or free from outside). See boiling mud pots, steam vents, and geysers right in the middle of the town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River (free). This is a moderate 3 km hike each way through geothermal landscape leading to a natural hot river where you can bathe. In January, the hike can be icy and snowy — wear proper footwear with grip. The contrast of soaking in warm geothermal water while surrounded by snow is magical.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and warm up. This is a great aurora night — Hveragerdi area has good dark sky access. If you are tired from the hike, monitor the aurora forecast from the resort and step outside if it becomes active.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the drive
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches for the hike — there are no facilities at Reykjadalur
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort, or try Varma restaurant in Hveragerdi for affordable Icelandic comfort food before driving back

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot spring hike is one of the best free hot spring experiences in Iceland. Bring a change of clothes and a dry bag for your belongings. The hike takes about 45-60 minutes each way. In January, start by 11:00 AM to have enough daylight. Trekking poles are recommended for icy conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hafnarfjordur, a charming town just south of Reykjavik known as the town of elves and hidden people (Huldufolk). Walk the old harbor area and explore the lava rock gardens. The Hafnarfjordur Museum (small fee) covers local history. The town is easily accessible by bus from Reykjavik.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a self-guided street art tour. Reykjavik has an impressive collection of murals and street art throughout the city, particularly in the 101 Reykjavik district. Pick up a free street art map from the tourist information center. Visit Grandi harbor district, a revitalized area with galleries, a flea market (Kolaportid on weekends), and the Saga Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Kolaportid Flea Market is open on weekends (Saturdays and Sundays) — if today is a weekend, this is an excellent place to find affordable Icelandic souvenirs, secondhand wool sweaters (lopapeysa), and local snacks. In the evening, take a Northern Lights bus tour from Reykjavik — these depart nightly when aurora conditions are favorable and cost around 5,000-7,000 ISK, with a free rebooking policy if no lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort
meals.lunch: Fish and chips from Reykjavik Fish restaurant near the old harbor — affordable and delicious fresh Icelandic fish
meals.dinner: Pho Viet, an affordable Vietnamese restaurant in Reykjavik, or self-catered dinner at the resort

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights bus tours are a good option if you do not have a rental car, as guides know the best dark sky locations and monitor forecasts in real time. Many companies like Reykjavik Excursions offer free rebooking if no aurora is seen. January offers some of the longest dark periods of the year, maximizing aurora viewing windows.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated aurora preparation and relaxation day. Sleep in after late-night aurora hunting. Visit Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach in Reykjavik (free or very small fee in winter). This artificial geothermal beach has warm water pumped in, creating a unique warm lagoon on the North Atlantic coast. Surreal in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping on a budget. Visit the Kolaportid Flea Market (open weekends) for the most affordable Icelandic souvenirs — wool products, Viking-themed items, and local snacks like dried fish (hardfiskur) and skyr. Alternatively, browse the Bonus supermarket for affordable edible souvenirs like Icelandic chocolate, licorice, and skyr powder.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated Northern Lights hunt. This is your last full evening — make it count. Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula lighthouse area (Reykjanesviti) or Thingvellir for maximum darkness. Bring all your warm gear, a tripod, and a wide-angle lens if available. Stay out from 20:00 to midnight if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — use up remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch at Cafe Loki near Hallgrimskirkja, famous for traditional Icelandic food including rye bread ice cream and lamb soup at moderate prices
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner — try Saegreifinn (The Sea Baron) near the old harbor for the famous lobster soup at around 2,500 ISK, a Reykjavik institution

day_by_day.notes: Nauthólsvík beach is one of Reykjavik's hidden gems and is free or very cheap to visit. The geothermal lagoon is around 15-19°C, much warmer than the surrounding sea. January is actually one of the statistically best months for Northern Lights in Iceland due to long nights. Keep checking the aurora forecast app obsessively on this final night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, store luggage at the hotel and take a final short walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to Iceland. Visit a nearby hot pot one last time if time permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, either head directly to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 30-45 minutes from the Reykjavik area) or squeeze in a final stop at the Bridge Between Continents or Reykjanes lighthouse for a last look at the dramatic Icelandic landscape. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of the Northern Lights, geothermal hot springs, dramatic waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes. The Flybus back to the airport is the most budget-friendly option.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast using remaining groceries or a bakery stop
meals.lunch: Airport food or a final gas station hot dog — keep it budget-friendly to the end
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips for the trip: Bonus supermarket groceries saved approximately 40-50% on food costs. Public swimming pools provided affordable hot spring experiences. Free attractions (waterfalls, national parks, coastal walks, street art) formed the backbone of the itinerary. A rental car shared among travelers was more cost-effective than tours for most day trips. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation: 8,000-12,000 ISK (approximately 55-85 USD) per person per day.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront room, and get a good night's rest. If skies are clear, step outside briefly – the resort's beachfront location offers a dark-sky vantage point for a spontaneous first glimpse of the Northern Lights.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on flight
meals.lunch: N/A – on flight
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from the airport's convenience kiosks or a vending machine at the resort upon arrival. Stock up on basics if a 24-hour shop is available near the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely light. Jet lag and late arrival mean rest is the priority. Confirm your resort transfer in advance (pre-booked shuttle or taxi ~45–60 min from KEF). Pack layers in your carry-on as Iceland in January is cold (−2°C to 3°C).

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a short walk along the beachfront to breathe in the crisp Arctic air and acclimate to Iceland's winter daylight (sunrise around 11:00 AM in January). Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik (approximately 40–50 min drive) for the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour. Explore the colorful streets of the city center, visit Hallgrímskirkja church, the old harbor, and sample traditional Icelandic bites like skyr, lamb soup, and rye bread ice cream with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by early evening. After dinner, bundle up and scan the skies from the beachfront for Northern Lights – January nights are long (darkness from ~4:00 PM), maximizing aurora chances. Check aurora forecast apps (Vedur.is) before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet – included or à la carte (~2,500–3,500 ISK). Enjoy skyr with berries and Icelandic rye bread.
meals.lunch: During the walking tour, sample street food and tasting stops included in the tour or grab a bowl of kjötsúpa (lamb soup) at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja (~1,800–2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Grillhúsið or a mid-range grill restaurant near the resort or Reykjavik. Try a lamb burger or fish and chips (~3,500–5,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour in advance. Tours typically run 2–3 hours. Wear waterproof boots and a windproof jacket. Sunrise is around 11:10 AM and sunset around 3:40 PM – plan the tour to maximize daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa, conveniently located near Keflavik (about 20 min from the resort area). Arrive at opening time (~8:00 AM) to beat crowds. Soak in the milky-blue geothermal waters surrounded by dramatic lava fields, enjoy the silica mud mask stations, and use the steam rooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at the Blue Lagoon or explore the surrounding lava field walking paths. Have lunch at the Lava Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon complex. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon and rest or explore the beachfront.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour – join a small-group tour departing from the Reykjavik/Keflavik area. Expert guides will drive to low-light-pollution zones to maximize aurora viewing chances. Tours typically run 3–4 hours starting around 8:00–9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departing early (~2,000 ISK). Alternatively, grab a pastry and coffee at a bakery near the Blue Lagoon entrance.
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon – mid-range options like fish soup, salads, and Icelandic lamb (~4,000–6,000 ISK). Book a table in advance.
meals.dinner: Early dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby casual spot before the Northern Lights tour. Try a hearty lamb stew or fish dish (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance – they sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. Comfort package (~12,000–15,000 ISK) includes towel, drink, and mask. Northern Lights tours are weather-dependent; operators will reschedule if conditions are poor.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from the late Northern Lights tour. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort. After breakfast, take a scenic coastal walk along the beachfront to watch the dramatic Atlantic waves and look for seabirds. Sunrise isn't until ~11:00 AM, so there's no rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a day trip to the Reykjanes Peninsula (30–40 min from the resort). Explore the Bridge Between Continents (where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet), the Gunnuhver hot spring geothermal area with its steaming mud pools, and the Reykjanes Lighthouse at Iceland's southwestern tip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for dinner. Spend the evening relaxing in the resort's facilities. If the sky is clear, try another self-guided Northern Lights watch from the dark beachfront after 9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – skyr parfait, eggs, Icelandic smoked salmon (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or stop at a petrol station café on the Reykjanes Peninsula (N1 stations serve surprisingly good soup and sandwiches, ~1,500–2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby seafood spot – try pan-fried Arctic char or cod with butter sauce (~4,000–5,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is free to explore independently. Gunnuhver is a short walk from the parking area. Dress in windproof layers – the peninsula is very exposed to Atlantic winds. Check if any volcanic activity is ongoing in the area as Reykjanes has been active in recent years.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the famous Golden Circle route (self-drive or guided day tour). First stop: Þingvellir National Park – a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the tectonic plates diverge and the world's first parliament (Alþing) was established in 930 AD. Walk the Almannagjá gorge in the crisp winter air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January, creating a stunning ice-and-water spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort (approximately 1.5–2 hours from Gullfoss). Arrive by early evening. Enjoy a warming dinner and check aurora forecasts for a possible late-night viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure (~2,500 ISK). Pack snacks and a thermos of hot coffee.
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café – warm lamb soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate (~2,500–3,500 ISK). Alternatively, pack your own picnic.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a local grill in the area – try a hearty beef or lamb burger with sweet potato fries (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from the resort area. Roads are generally well-maintained but check road conditions at road.is before departing. A 4WD rental is recommended in January. Allow 8–9 hours total for the full loop.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day – sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning at the resort's spa or wellness facilities. Read, relax, and recharge after two busy days of sightseeing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approximately 1.5 hours from the resort). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891, surrounded by geothermal activity, small geysers, and steaming vents. A much more intimate and affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening (~6:00–7:00 PM). Enjoy a relaxed dinner. Keep the evening free for potential Northern Lights viewing – the Secret Lagoon area's rural setting means you may have already seen some on the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – take your time (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or pack a sandwich for the road.
meals.dinner: Try a local restaurant near Flúðir before heading back, or dine at the resort. Consider trying plokkfiskur (Icelandic fish stew with potatoes) (~3,000–4,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,000–3,500 ISK per person – much more affordable than the Blue Lagoon. Bring a swimsuit, towel (or rent one), and flip-flops. The outdoor pool is open year-round and the contrast of cold air and warm water is magical in January.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the South Coast day trip – one of Iceland's most scenic drives. Head east along Route 1. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can walk behind the curtain of water (may be icy/closed in January – check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for dramatic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara (near Vík) – admire the dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the charming village of Vík í Mýrdal and its hilltop church. Then head to Glacier Hiking on Sólheimajökull – strap on crampons and explore the glacier with a certified guide (2–3 hour tour).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward the resort (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Vík). Arrive around 8:00–9:00 PM. Grab a late dinner and wind down.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the long day (~2,500 ISK). Pack snacks and water.
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant near Reynisfjara or a café in Vík – try fish soup or a lamb wrap (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort or a nearby spot – a warming bowl of soup and bread or a pizza (~3,000–4,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day (10–12 hours of driving and activities). Depart by 9:00–10:00 AM to make the most of limited daylight (roughly 11:00 AM–3:30 PM). Glacier hiking requires booking in advance – Sólheimajökull tours typically depart at 11:00 AM or 1:00 PM. Wear waterproof pants and sturdy boots; crampons and helmets are provided.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day after the demanding South Coast trip. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a gentle stroll along the resort's beachfront. Catch up on journaling, photos, or simply enjoy the dramatic winter seascape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik independently. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn) to learn about Iceland's history from settlement to modern times (~2,000 ISK entry). Stroll Laugavegur shopping street for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), design items, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a proper Reykjavik dinner experience before returning to the resort. Consider attending a live music venue or a local bar to experience Reykjavik's vibrant nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Slow resort breakfast (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Bergsson Mathús or similar café in Reykjavik – open-faced sandwiches, salads, and soups (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) or a mid-range Reykjavik restaurant – try sushi-style Icelandic fish dishes or a tasting menu (~6,000–9,000 ISK per person for a special evening).

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik museums are a great option for January days when weather is harsh. The National Museum is centrally located and very well curated. Laugavegur street has a mix of budget and mid-range shops. Tipping is not customary in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Second Northern Lights Guided Tour – book a different operator or the same tour on a new night to increase your chances of a clear-sky sighting. Some tours depart in the late afternoon in January (around 5:00–6:00 PM) when darkness falls early. Spend the morning relaxing at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark area. Explore the Svartsengi geothermal power plant area (exterior views), the lava fields of the 2021–2024 Fagradalsfjall eruptions (check safety status), and the Bridge Between Continents if not visited earlier.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour (evening departure ~8:00 PM). Guides use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to drive to the best viewing locations. Dress in your warmest layers – temperatures can drop to −10°C with wind chill.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Café or soup restaurant near the Reykjanes area or pack your own (~1,500–2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Early dinner at the resort before the Northern Lights tour. Try a warming lamb or beef stew (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January has the highest statistical chance for Northern Lights in Iceland due to long dark nights. KP index of 3+ is ideal. Download the 'My Aurora Forecast' app. Even if the guided tour doesn't produce sightings, the experience of standing under Iceland's winter sky is magical.

day_by_day.morning: Take a relaxed morning and visit the Keflavik area's local swimming pool (sundlaug) – Icelandic public pools are a beloved cultural institution with hot tubs (heitur pottur), steam rooms, and lanes. Entry is very affordable (~1,000–1,200 ISK) and a great way to mingle with locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula for a scenic afternoon excursion (approximately 2 hours from the resort). Visit the dramatic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (immortalized by Jules Verne), the Arnarstapi coastal cliffs, and the charming fishing village of Grundarfjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive toward the resort (2–2.5 hours). The drive back offers potential Northern Lights sightings if skies are clear. Arrive at the resort by 9:00–10:00 PM for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast (~2,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Arnarstapi or a local café in Grundarfjörður – fresh fish soup and Icelandic bread (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Late resort dinner or a takeaway pizza/burger (~3,000–4,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a long day trip – consider an early start or an overnight if you wish to explore more. In January, roads to Snæfellsnes can be challenging; check road.is. The peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' for its diverse landscapes. Kirkjufell mountain near Grundarfjörður is one of Iceland's most photographed peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning at the resort. Enjoy breakfast with ocean views. Pack for a half-day Reykjavik cultural exploration. Visit Harpa Concert Hall (free to enter the lobby – stunning geometric glass architecture) and the waterfront Sculpture & Shore Walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavik Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) or the Perlan museum – a futuristic glass dome with exhibitions on Iceland's nature, a real ice cave, and a panoramic viewing deck (~3,500 ISK). Grab coffee at one of Reykjavik's cozy specialty coffee shops on Skólavörðustígur street.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt – either a self-guided drive into the dark countryside near the resort or book a last-minute guided tour if forecasts look promising. Celebrate the trip with a special dinner in Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Cozy café near Harpa or Laugavegur – try a Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur (~500 ISK) and a bowl of soup (~1,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Special dinner at Messinn or Snaps Bistro in Reykjavik – excellent mid-range Icelandic cuisine with fresh fish and lamb (~5,000–7,500 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Perlan's ice cave exhibition is a great alternative if you didn't do glacier hiking or want an indoor experience. The hot dog stand Bæjarins Beztu is a Reykjavik institution – even Bill Clinton ate there! Book dinner reservations in advance for popular Reykjavik restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning in Iceland – enjoy a long, indulgent resort breakfast. Take a final beachfront walk to soak in the raw Icelandic coastal scenery. Pack non-essential items and prepare luggage for departure the next day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a final soak if you wish (book in advance) or visit the nearby Svartsengi area for a peaceful walk among the lava fields. Alternatively, revisit Reykjavik for any last-minute souvenir shopping on Laugavegur – pick up Icelandic wool products, lava salt, dried fish, and Brennivín schnapps.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort or at a restaurant near the airport area. Reflect on the trip, review photos, and prepare for the journey home. Pack your carry-on with duty-free purchases and any perishable Icelandic snacks for the flight.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – treat yourself to the full spread (~3,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Reykjavik café or the resort – soup, sandwich, or skyr (~2,000–2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range restaurant. Order a classic Icelandic lamb rack with root vegetables (~5,000–7,000 ISK) and toast with a local craft beer or Brennivín.

day_by_day.notes: Keflavik Airport has good duty-free shopping – Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skincare products (Blue Lagoon brand) are popular purchases. Confirm your flight time and arrange airport transfer. Luggage storage may be available at the resort for the final afternoon if checkout is early.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final Icelandic breakfast at the resort or a nearby café. Transfer to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 30–45 minutes from the resort). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs. If time allows, visit the Viking World Museum near the airport (Víkingaheimar) – a fascinating small museum with a reconstructed Viking ship (~2,500 ISK, 15 min from airport).
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or airport café – skyr, pastry, and strong Icelandic coffee (~2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight or upon arrival at home destination.

day_by_day.notes: Keflavik Airport is modern and well-equipped. Security lines can be long in peak periods – arrive early. Iceland's VAT refund (for purchases over 6,000 ISK) can be claimed at the airport before security. Keep all receipts from Icelandic purchases. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the Arctic sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind this magical phenomenon.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic geothermal hot spring surrounded by dramatic lava fields. The milky-blue mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin-healing silica and algae. Book the Comfort package to include a silica mud mask and a welcome drink.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents, offering an authentic and affordable soak in the Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Glacier Hiking on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the stunning Sólheimajökull glacier with a certified guide. Trek across ice formations, peer into vivid blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. A thrilling activity that pairs perfectly with the surrounding volcanic scenery.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and rich Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, and fresh seafood, while visiting landmarks such as Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity – warm skyr with Icelandic honey and a glass of Brennivín – and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: In-flight
meals.lunch: In-flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter prepared by the resort chef upon arrival – smoked lamb, skyr mousse, dark rye bread, and Icelandic butter.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm all upcoming bookings with the resort concierge before retiring. January nights are long (~19 hours of darkness), ideal for Northern Lights sightings – keep an eye on the sky from your suite's private terrace.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter light. Breathe the Arctic air and photograph the coastline at the brief midday golden hour (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30 in January).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 20 minutes from the resort by private transfer). Book the exclusive Retreat Spa package – private lagoon access, in-water massages, algae mask ritual, and a float in the iconic milky-blue 38–40°C waters surrounded by volcanic lava fields. Enjoy the Lava Restaurant within the complex for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. After sunset (~15:30), join the Northern Lights Guided Tour – a small-group excursion departing from the resort area into darkness away from light pollution. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasting apps. Wrap up in provided thermal suits and sip hot chocolate under the dancing green curtains of the Aurora Borealis.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet – Icelandic pastries, smoked salmon, skyr, fresh-pressed juices, and Arabica pour-over coffee.
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon – langoustine soup, pan-seared Arctic char, and house-made lava bread with butter.
meals.dinner: Back at the resort's signature restaurant – slow-roasted reindeer tenderloin with root vegetable purée, paired with a curated Icelandic craft beer flight.

day_by_day.notes: January aurora activity can be strong (KP index permitting). The tour guide will monitor forecasts and may adjust departure time to maximize sighting probability. Dress in resort-provided thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided sunrise photography session along the resort's beachfront (golden hour light arrives around 11:00). A professional photographer from the resort accompanies you to capture sea stacks, black sand, and dramatic winter skies. Breakfast in-room via butler service beforehand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour – a private premium version of this guided experience. Explore the colorful streets of Reykjavik, visit Hallgrímskirkja church, browse the Kolaportið flea market (if open), sample fermented shark (hákarl), hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu, and artisan chocolates. Stop at the National Museum for a curated Viking heritage briefing.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner reservation at Dill Restaurant (Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant) in Reykjavik – a Nordic tasting menu celebrating hyper-local, seasonal Icelandic ingredients. Private transfer to and from the city.

meals.breakfast: In-room butler breakfast – warm oatmeal with crowberries, Icelandic eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: During the walking tour – curated tastings across multiple Reykjavik food stops (langoustine tails, lamb soup, artisan cheese, and Icelandic flatbread).
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik – 7-course Nordic tasting menu with optional Icelandic wine and aquavit pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Dill Restaurant well in advance as it is extremely popular. The private walking tour can be customized through the resort concierge to focus more on Viking history or culinary stops per your preference.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Golden Circle private luxury tour begins after a hearty breakfast. First stop: Þingvellir National Park – walk the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, visit the site of the world's first parliament (Alþing, 930 AD), and admire frozen waterfalls and ice-draped lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area – witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 30 meters into the Arctic sky. Then visit Gullfoss Waterfall, Iceland's most powerful cascade, partially frozen in winter and extraordinarily dramatic. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef in a heated vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Unwind in the resort's private hot tub or geothermal pool with views of the dark sky. Northern Lights watch from the resort terrace with a private butler on standby with warm drinks.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – full Icelandic breakfast: lamb sausages, rye bread, smoked trout, skyr parfait, and Valhalla coffee blend.
meals.lunch: Gourmet heated picnic box prepared by resort chef – thermos of lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, Icelandic cheese, and dark chocolate.
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant – pan-seared halibut with dill cream, pickled cucumber, and seaweed butter, followed by skyr cheesecake with bilberry compote.

day_by_day.notes: January roads on the Golden Circle are generally accessible but can be icy. The private driver will have a 4WD luxury SUV with studded tires. Allow flexibility for weather delays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approximately 1.5 hours from the resort by private transfer). Arrive early for an exclusive pre-opening private soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool (est. 1891), naturally heated to 38–40°C. The surrounding geothermal vents bubble and steam in the winter cold – a truly otherworldly scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the small village of Flúðir and nearby mushroom farms and greenhouse tomato farms that thrive on geothermal energy. Return toward the resort, stopping at Kerið volcanic crater lake – a 3,000-year-old caldera with vivid red, black, and white volcanic rock contrasting against the frozen teal lake surface.
day_by_day.evening: Private Northern Lights Guided Tour (second attempt/dedicated session). Tonight's tour ventures further inland toward the Reykjanes Peninsula highlands for darker skies. Guides provide astrophotography coaching and tripod setups for long-exposure aurora shots.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – smoked salmon bagel, Icelandic yogurt with granola, fresh fruit plate, and cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Matur og Drykkur restaurant in Reykjavik (en route) – traditional Icelandic cuisine reimagined: cod head, salted lamb, and rye bread ice cream.
meals.dinner: Resort private dining experience – butler-served four-course dinner in your beachfront suite with candlelight and curated wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon private early access must be arranged in advance through the resort concierge. Kerið crater has a small admission fee. Dress warmly in multiple thermal layers for the evening aurora tour.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter tour of the Reykjanes Peninsula and surrounding lava fields (departing from a nearby helipad). Aerial views of geothermal hotspots, dramatic coastlines, the Bridge Between Continents, and (weather permitting) the Blue Lagoon from above. Approximately 45–60 minutes of flight time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bridge Between Continents on the Reykjanes Peninsula – walk across the symbolic footbridge spanning the gap between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Explore the Reykjanes Geopark, UNESCO-recognized, with boiling mud pools, sulfur vents, and dramatic lava formations.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Book an in-room couple's or solo luxury spa treatment – Icelandic volcanic stone massage, algae body wrap, or Arctic facial using local ingredients. Dine at the resort's beachfront lounge.

meals.breakfast: In-room butler service – eggs any style, Icelandic pastries, fresh-squeezed juice, and a selection of Icelandic cheeses.
meals.lunch: Kaffi Duus restaurant in Keflavík – fresh lobster soup, open-faced shrimp sandwiches, and Icelandic craft beer.
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront lounge – grilled catch-of-the-day (likely cod or haddock) with lemon butter, roasted root vegetables, and a bottle of white Burgundy.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are highly weather-dependent in January. The resort concierge should have a backup land-based activity ready (e.g., lava field ATV tour or private geothermal cave visit). Book the helicopter well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day South Coast adventure. Depart early by private luxury 4WD. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall – walk behind the cascading falls (may be partially frozen in January, creating spectacular ice formations). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall – climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Glacier Hiking on Sólheimajökull – strap on crampons and harness provided by certified guides. Trek across the glacier's blue-ice ridges, peer into crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This is a thrilling, immersive premium experience with a private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Drive along the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara – dramatic basalt sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), hexagonal basalt columns, and roaring Atlantic surf. Explore the black sand beach safely (rogue waves are a serious hazard – stay behind the safety markers). Return to resort for a warm dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – energy-rich: porridge with Icelandic honey, protein-packed skyr, whole grain toast, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the heated private vehicle – resort-prepared thermos of lamb soup, smoked lamb wraps, Icelandic chocolate, and hot tea.
meals.dinner: Strondin Bistro & Bar (or similar South Coast restaurant) – fresh langoustine, grilled lamb chops, and Icelandic craft spirits before the drive back.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires moderate fitness. Certified guides provide all safety equipment. January conditions on the glacier can be icy – guides will assess safety on the day. Reynisfjara beach is notoriously dangerous; follow all guide and signage warnings strictly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and spend time in the resort's private geothermal pool or hot tub. Read, journal, or simply stargaze during the brief midday light. Optional: light yoga or stretching session with the resort's wellness instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Icelandic cooking class with the resort's head chef. Learn to prepare traditional Icelandic dishes: skyr-marinated lamb, rye bread baked in geothermal ground (hverabrauð), langoustine bisque, and Icelandic kleina doughnuts. Take home a handwritten recipe card.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the resort's dedicated aurora observation deck. The resort provides heated outdoor loungers, thermal blankets, hot chocolate, and a star-gazing guide who identifies constellations and explains aurora science. If aurora activity is high, this is one of the most magical settings imaginable.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – leisurely full breakfast with all Icelandic favorites plus a mimosa or fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort lounge – lobster bisque, open-faced smoked salmon sandwich, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the afternoon cooking class, enjoyed at a private candlelit table set by the resort team – a uniquely personal dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: This is a purposeful rest day to recharge mid-trip. The cooking class is a premium add-on to be arranged with the resort in advance. Aurora activity in January averages 4–5 visible nights per week on the Reykjanes Peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Private snowmobile tour on a glacier (transfer to Langjökull glacier, Iceland's second-largest, approximately 2 hours by private vehicle). Strap into a premium snowmobile and race across the vast white expanse of the glacier with a certified guide. Optional: enter the man-made ice tunnel inside Langjökull for an extraordinary ice cave experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Borgarnes – a series of springs bubbling up through ancient lava fields and cascading into the Hvítá River, partially frozen in January and hauntingly beautiful. Explore the Borgarnes Settlement Center for an immersive Viking saga exhibition.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private hot spring soak and a sunset (approximately 15:30) cocktail on the beachfront terrace. Dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – high-energy for snowmobiling: eggs, lamb sausages, dark bread, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Hótel Húsafell restaurant (near Langjökull) – locally sourced Icelandic menu with reindeer stew, fresh-baked bread, and bilberry dessert.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – dry-aged Icelandic lamb rack with rosemary jus, truffle mashed potato, and a bottle of premium Burgundy red.

day_by_day.notes: Langjökull snowmobile tours require advance booking with a specialist operator. The ice tunnel inside the glacier is a separate ticketed experience but absolutely worth including. January road conditions may require the 4WD to take a longer route – build in buffer time.

day_by_day.morning: Private whale watching tour from Reykjavík Old Harbour (approximately 40 minutes from resort). January sightings include humpback whales, minke whales, and white-beaked dolphins. Board a premium small-group vessel with heated cabins, on-board marine biologist, and hot drinks. Dress in provided flotation suits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavík independently or with a private guide. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall (architectural masterpiece), the Sun Voyager sculpture, the Saga Museum for a wax figure Viking experience, and browse the luxury boutiques on Laugavegur street for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), lava jewelry, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Geysir Bistro & Bar or Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavík – Iceland's premier steakhouse featuring dry-aged Icelandic beef, lamb, and fresh seafood cooked over open lava stone grills. Private transfer back to resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – smoked trout on dark rye, skyr with seasonal berries, and Icelandic pastries.
meals.lunch: Messinn restaurant in Reykjavík – famous for cast-iron pan-served fresh fish of the day with Icelandic sides.
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn, Reykjavík – dry-aged Icelandic beef fillet, lobster tail, and a premium Icelandic craft spirits pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching is weather and sea-condition dependent. The tour operator will assess conditions on the day. January can be rough at sea – motion sickness patches are recommended. The resort concierge can arrange a backup activity (e.g., private art gallery tour or spa day) if the tour is cancelled.

day_by_day.morning: Private ice cave exploration tour in Þórsmörk or the Katla volcanic system (approximately 2–2.5 hours from resort). These natural blue-ice caves are only accessible in winter and each one is unique. A certified glacier guide leads you through shimmering blue tunnels, ice formations, and volcanic ash layers inside the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Skógar Folk Museum – an extraordinary open-air museum with turf houses, a church, and thousands of artifacts documenting Icelandic rural life over centuries. Walk the short trail to Skógafoss for a second visit in different light conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated aurora hunting evening with a premium private Northern Lights guide. Tonight's route is customized based on the evening's weather forecast and aurora activity (KP index). Travel up to 100km from the resort if needed for clear skies. Champagne toast under the aurora.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – full spread with freshly baked Icelandic bread, smoked lamb, and skyr.
meals.lunch: Hotel Skógafoss restaurant (near the waterfall) – lamb soup, fresh-baked bread, and Icelandic dairy dessert.
meals.dinner: Resort private dining – seven-course tasting menu prepared by the resort chef, served in the resort's exclusive private dining room with floor-to-ceiling ocean views.

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours require advance booking and are dependent on glacier safety conditions assessed by guides on the day. The Katla ice cave is particularly spectacular due to black volcanic ash layers contrasting with blue ice. This is a highlight not to miss.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning at the resort. Indulge in a premium spa morning – full-body Icelandic volcanic mud treatment, hot stone massage, and Arctic facial. Spend time in the resort's infinity geothermal pool overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private horseback riding on Icelandic horses – a unique breed known for their extra gait (tölt), small stature, and gentle temperament. Ride along the dramatic Reykjanes coastline and lava fields with a private guide. Icelandic horses are exceptionally sure-footed on icy terrain.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest table – a private chef's table experience in the kitchen or a reserved window table overlooking the ocean. A personalized menu celebrating the best of Icelandic cuisine: langoustine, Arctic char, lamb, skyr, and Icelandic spirits. The resort sommelier presents a curated wine journey.

meals.breakfast: In-room butler breakfast – final Icelandic morning feast: all your favorites from the week, served with a bottle of Icelandic sparkling water and fresh flowers.
meals.lunch: Resort lounge light lunch – lobster rolls, Icelandic chips, and a glass of Chablis.
meals.dinner: Resort chef's table farewell dinner – bespoke 8-course tasting menu with premium wine pairing, ending with a hand-crafted Icelandic chocolate box as a parting gift.

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic horses are gentle and suitable for all riding abilities. The horseback tour operator should be briefed on your experience level in advance. This evening is the emotional highlight of the trip – request any special dietary preferences or celebratory touches (e.g., anniversary setup) with the resort in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake early for one last soak in the resort's private geothermal hot tub as the Arctic darkness gives way to the brief golden sunrise (around 11:00). Pack, check out, and collect any purchased Icelandic souvenirs arranged by the concierge (lopapeysa sweaters, lava salt, skyr skincare products, Icelandic music).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional final stop at the Blue Lagoon Comfort package for a 2-hour farewell soak and silica mud mask before heading to Keflavík Airport (15 minutes away). Private luxury transfer to the airport with all luggage handled by resort staff.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Board your flight home carrying memories of dancing auroras, steaming hot springs, ancient glaciers, and the wild, otherworldly beauty of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Resort final breakfast – skyr parfait, smoked salmon, dark rye bread, and a farewell coffee from the resort barista.
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant (if time allows) – langoustine soup and Icelandic flatbread, or airport lounge dining at Keflavík.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at airport lounge.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time should be negotiated as late as possible (ideally 14:00) with the resort to maximize your final morning. The Blue Lagoon is only 10 minutes from Keflavík Airport, making it a perfect final stop. Confirm all private transfer timings the evening before to ensure a stress-free departure.
